text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000158 bills 99215 at about three times the risk-adjusted expectation, but the excess is concentrated in multi-morbid patients and the thin documentation sample does not contradict the billed levels.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share rises steeply with condition count, and most 99215 claims fall on patients with four or more chronic conditions (e.g., C0086184, C0086638). Only a small share fall on 0–1 condition patients, which is closer to a complex-panel pattern than to indiscriminate upcoding. However, the provider's share exceeds the all-provider rate at every complexity level, including low-complexity visits such as C0086547 (acute URI, no chronic conditions) and C0086619 (follow-up only). So patient mix alone may not explain the full excess. The three documented 99215 claims (C0086244, C0086324, C0086658) supported high MDM, and no notes showed data-review inflation without a test line. Still, three charts is far too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding, and the heavy 99214 volume is also worth noting. A reviewer should first request records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, then pull a larger random sample of 99215 charts to test whether high MDM holds up beyond these three."}
